newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures settle higher on late jump.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures settle higher on late jump.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Wednesday on a late surge of buying activity despite softer cash market prices and outlook of mild weather continuing in the western U.S.
"It was just aggressive buying toward the end," said a trader in Houston.
Brokers and traders said futures prices began to climb in tandem with stronger bids which emerged in afternoon physical and over-the-counter (OTC) trading.
In late OTC activity, December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were assessed at $23.25-$23.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) and December Palo Verde (PV) at $21.55-$22.05.
"Today physicals and gas were down, but power was up," another Houston trader said.
December natural gas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub was quoted at $2.36-$2.37 per million British thermal units, better bid than Tuesday's $2.32-$2.37.
December COB futures settled at its session high of $23.50, up 45 cents from Tuesday's close.
January COB finished up 56 cents at $21.00. Deferred COB months ended flat to 56 cents higher.
December PV futures settled at $21.80, up 75 cents after traded between $21.25 and $21.85.
January PV finished at $19.50, up 20 cents. Outer PV contracts ended 25 to 50 cents higher.
Brokers and traders expected the complex to trade within its recent range until fresh fundamentals develop.

The latest forecasts showed the Pacific Northwest would experience seasonal temperatures through the end of the week, and the Southwest would enjoy slightly warmer than normal weather during the same period.
